instructions: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water for about 30 seconds. Transfer it to a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt, and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take the pan off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes.
Put the cashews in a small bowl with 1/2 cup warm water and leave them for 10 minutes. Drain, then blend them with 1/4 cup fresh water until smooth and set the paste aside.
Meanwhile, wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them 1/4 inch thick. Finely chop the onion, grate the ginger and mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, cover and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it is soft and golden at the edges.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato puree, turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, 1 tsp of the salt, the mushrooms and 1/2 cup water. Stir, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom of the pan.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the mushrooms are cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Crush the fenugreek leaves between your palms over the pan. Stir in the cashew paste and 1/4 cup chopped cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Ministry of Curry leads (onion softened first, then ginger, garlic, tomato and spices with the mushrooms cooked covered, finished with fenugreek leaves and a cashew paste). Its stovetop method was used, with oil in place of ghee so the dish is vegan, and the chili is the mild Kashmiri kind. Playful Cooking and Greenbowl2soul confirm the onion and tomato base, and some versions blend it smooth; the lead's chunky gravy was kept.
